title: The Two Brothers and the Field (Español)

keywords: the two brothers and the field
full_text:
Two farmer brothers, Somanna and Bhimanna, came before King Krishnadevaraya’s court, arguing furiously over the inheritance of a fertile five-acre agricultural field left by their late father.
Somanna shouted: 'The eastern half has the canal water; it belongs to me by birthright!'
Bhimanna yelled: 'The western half has rich black soil; our father promised it to me on his deathbed!'

They produced contradictory witnesses, spent their savings on dishonest lawyers, and neglected the land completely, until the once-blooming field became overgrown with thorny weeds and scrub.

The King, exhausted by their endless bickering, turned to Tenali Raman:
'Tenali, settle this dispute equitably, for they have disrupted the court for three months.'

Tenali had both brothers brought before him. He asked:
'Brothers, have you asked the field itself to whom it wishes to belong?'
The brothers stared: 'Can a patch of dirt speak?'
Tenali replied solemnly:
'The Earth is a living mother; she speaks to those who listen. Let us go to the field at sunset.'

At the field, Tenali knelt upon the soil, placed his ear against the dry ground, and listened intently for ten minutes while the brothers watched in silence.

Tenali stood up, brushing dirt from his knees, with a sorrowful expression:
'Brothers, I heard the field speaking clearly.'
Somanna asked eagerly: 'What did she say? Did she award the land to me?'
Bhimanna asked: 'Did she name me her owner?'

Tenali answered:
'The field was laughing aloud with bitter mockery!
She said: "Behold these two foolish brothers! For ten generations, their ancestors claimed they owned me; each man died, turned to dust, and became part of my soil, while I remained here eternal and unchanged!
Today, these two sons fight and bleed over who owns me, yet neither of them has planted a single seed of corn or given me a drop of water for a whole year!
Tell them: I belong not to the man who waves a stamped paper of ownership, but to the hands that till my soil, plant seeds with love, and feed the hungry with honest sweat!"'

The two brothers stood in stunned silence.
Tenali’s profound words pierced through their selfish arrogance like an arrow of light.
They looked at the neglected, weed-choked field that had fed their ancestors for centuries, and tears of shame filled their eyes.

Somanna embraced Bhimanna, dropping their lawsuits on the spot.
They agreed to divide the work equally, sharing water and soil as partners. Within a season, the field was green with bumper crops of golden paddy, proving that true ownership is earned through loving care, not angry contention.
moral: Earth yields its treasure not to legal squabbles, but to honest labor that nurtures it with love. [ES]
